newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WADDLE RETURNS TO NORTH-EAST WITH SUNDERLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WADDLE RETURNS TO NORTH-EAST WITH SUNDERLAND.

text.p: Chris Waddle, who began his professional career with Newcastle United almost 17 years ago, signed for his boyhood idols Sunderland for 75,000 pounds ($120,000) on Monday.

The 36-year-old former international winger, who won 62 caps for England between 1985 and 1992, moved from Bradford City, struggling at the foot of the first division to Sunderland, in a similar plight near the bottom of the premier league.

He has signed an initial contract with the club until the end of the season and the move fulfils a long-cherished dream as he was a Sunderland fan as a boy, even though he started his professional career with their arch-rivals.
Waddle left Sheffield Wednesday for Bradford City at the start of the season and has been in outstanding form for the Yorkshire side despite their poor form in the first division.

Although a move to Nottingham Forest broke down last week and he pulled out of Bradford's side for the match against Reading on Saturday, he leaves with the blessings of Bradford coach Chris Kamara who said he was very disappointed to sell him.

Waddle began his senior career at minor league Tow Law Town in his teens when he also worked in a sausage-making factory. He moved to Newcastle for 1,000 pounds ($1,600) in 1980 and played 190 matches for Newcastle before moving to Tottenham (1985) for 590,000 pounds ($944,000), Marseille (1989) for 4.2 million pounds ($6.7 million) and Sheffield Wednesday (1992) for 1.0 million pounds ($1.6 million).
On January 25 Waddle scored a superb goal, firing a shot past Everton goalkeeper Neville Southall from 40 metres, an effort that could earn him the award for goal of the season in May.
Ironically, Sunderland's last home match of the season on May 4 is at home to Everton.
